writeup.headline: Innodata rates Hold: fast growth and a debt-free balance sheet, offset by a weak share-price trend.
writeup.thesis: INNODATA scores 62, a Hold, just 3 points short of the Buy band. Growth is the standout at 91, with revenue up 57.8% year on year in the latest quarter and growth that sped up by 3.4 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 100 with net cash and no debt, and quality scores 69 on a 42.7% gross margin, an 18.2% operating margin and a normalised FCF margin of 21.2%. Holding the score back is the trend factor at 20: the stock is 56.3% below its 52-week high and 14.0% below its 200-day average, though it is 10.7 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation scores 43. In absolute terms, multiples of 5.8x sales and 27.4x EV/EBIT are fairly high, and the normalised FCF yield is 1.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. P/S is near the middle of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: High customer concentration, with the top customer at 37% of Q2 revenue
Reported FCF of $124.3M in the June quarter far exceeded revenue of $92.1M, and the cause is not in the tagged data, so it may not repeat
Competition in AI training data, including Meta's stake in Scale AI
Weak price momentum: down 33.4% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, with heavy insider selling over the past 12 months
Upcoming early-November earnings must support the 40%+ FY2026 revenue growth guidance
what_would_change: A 3-point gain in the score, for example from a recovering share-price trend or confirmed large new programs, would move it to Buy
A miss or cut to the 40%+ growth guidance would weaken the growth score and could pull the rating lower
A drop of 18 points to below 45, such as from sharp growth deceleration plus negative news, would be needed for Sell
